authority: the hub's pinned wrangler npx cache (BH-9460)
note: state/wrangler-npx/: a private npm cache holding one installed wrangler, so a worker deploy step never installs wrangler itself. bin/lib/wrangler-run.sh wrangler_install writes .stage.<pid>, renames it to v<version>-<epoch>/ (with .spec and .version) and swaps the `current` symlink by rename, under locks/wrangler-install.lock; .install-failed holds `<epoch> <spec>` of the last failed install. Retention: `current` and the previous version dir stay, older version dirs and stale stage dirs are deleted by each install run. Losing it costs one reinstall; until then wrangler_run uses the shared npx cache. Machine-local, never carried

authority: the npm code of the last wrangler tool failure (BH-9460)
note: state/wrangler-tool-error: one line, the npm error code (ENOTEMPTY, ...) of the last wrangler_run that returned rc 87, written tmp+mv by bin/lib/wrangler-run.sh and read by wrangler_tool_code_last for the alert text of bin/harness-sync.sh. One overwritten file, no growth. Losing it makes the next alert say `unknown`

state/worker-stale-paged/<worker>: the epoch of the last LIVE WORKER IS STALE page bin/harness-sync.sh worker_stale_page wrote for that worker, so the page repeats at most once per HARNESS_SYNC_WORKER_STALE_PAGE_S. Written tmp+mv, removed by the next good deploy of that worker. One file per worker, no growth. Losing it costs one repeated page
